answer: Latency-fingerprint bonds. Each identity posts a 500-token bond before its voyage into the registry; replies carry timing jitter, and listeners log prompt-to-answer gaps. When two identities answer the same relayed prompt sequence with gaps within 40 ms, like echoes off one canyon wall, a challenger files both traces and claims 15% of each bond, the rest burns. Clones trail an operator like a comet's tail, but each correlated reply is exposure: at 20% per-epoch odds, expected loss is 0.3x500x0.2 = 30 tokens per clone per epoch vs 20 earned, so extra clones drain value.
